author: IGN
description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Xbox Business Strategist Brandon Stirrup caused a firestorm on Twitter recently, admitting that he used AI to create a "little bad game" all on his own. This was to prove his point that AI tools are more widely used in the video game industry than it lets on, considering how anti-AI the gaming public tends to be. Stirrup's hope is that the industry will get over the stigma of AI and just admit that it's now part of the development workflow. Of course, comments weren't necessarily kind to him, and he deleted his Twitter account shortly after, but not before the internet screengrabbed his tweets and plastered them all over Reddit. But he's not necessarily wrong—Unreal Engine has AI tools built in, and Epic Games is coding their new Star Wars shooter solely with AI. Speaking of Star Wars, Lucasfilm is rumored to be approaching several studios to work on Battlefront 3, with DICE, Respawn, and Bungie being the supposed frontrunners. And we’re riding Mine Cart Madness
title: Xbox Staffer Claims Games Industry Is "Pretending to Not Use A.I." - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
Final Fantasy Resonance reviewed by Michael Higham on Nintendo Switch 2.

"Part of playing through Final Fantasy Resonance is to examine why an older era of RPG was wedged into our psyche for so long. The rose-tinted glasses can be strong at times, but so too was the sharpness of their messages, and the ones we remember most fondly understood that simple did not mean shallow. And that's the biggest thing Resonance couldn't really nail down. Even with weaker dialogue that fills large stretches of its story, the journey is still worth embarking on. Resonance is special for how it wields HD-2D as an art style to set a new, higher standard that goes well beyond nostalgia. It's the flair that makes a solid turn-based combat system more satisfying when beating down a staggered boss. And it's what paints its world as an exciting place to explore, especially when a superb soundtrack backs up each moment before hitting you with a nasty battle theme. Although I'm left underwhelmed by pieces of
title: Final Fantasy Resonance Video Review

FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE also pays tribute to all the games in the mainline FINAL FANTASY franchise with recruitable “visions” in the forms of classic characters like Cloud, Terra and Clive who can join battles and unleash special moves.
 
Gameplay captured on Switch 2
